Install, update and find your worlds

Each installer builds the game from source and adds a launcher. Player worlds, editable data and shared preferences live outside the versioned application payloads; updates preserve them.

Voxelgame main dd29d91 · 4 min read · Everyone · feature ledger · all guides

Before you install

You need an internet connection, several GB of free disk space and a working Vulkan graphics driver. On Linux the game runs in an X11 or XWayland session; it has no native Wayland window.

Tip. Keep the extracted source folder until setup finishes. You can delete it afterwards.

Install on Linux

  1. Open a terminal in the extracted source folder.
  2. Run bash install.sh as your normal user. Do not use sudo; setup only uses it for system packages.
  3. Read the plan and confirm it. First setup installs compiler/audio tools and Rust, builds the game and adds a launcher. Existing Linux installations reuse their tools without administrator prompts; repair missing prerequisites separately.
  4. Start Voxelgame from the application menu.
Key or actionWhat it does
--yesAccept the plan without asking
--prefix PATHInstall the app into another folder
--skip-prerequisitesSkip the tool install; use this on other distributions after installing the tools yourself (see docs/INSTALLING.md)
--helpShow the options; changes nothing

Setup never starts the game and never touches existing worlds.

Install on Windows

Careful. The Windows installer has not been tested on a real Windows PC yet.
  1. Double-click install-windows.cmd.
  2. Confirm the plan. If Windows asks, approve the Microsoft C++ Build Tools installer.
  3. Wait while setup downloads any missing Build Tools, Rust and FFmpeg, then builds the game.
  4. Start Voxelgame from the Start menu. The shortcut has no Voxelgame icon.

If the compiler setup asks you to restart Windows, restart it and run the installer again. Managed PCs may need an administrator to allow PowerShell scripts. In PowerShell, run install-windows.ps1 with the same options as the Linux installer: -Yes or -Prefix PATH.

Install on macOS

Careful. The macOS build is not validated yet. Graphics and sound are untested, and the game may fail to start on some Macs.
  1. Double-click Install-macOS.command and press Return to accept the plan.
  2. If Apple offers the Command Line Tools installer, finish it.
  3. If Homebrew asks for your password, enter your Mac password.
  4. Open Voxelgame.app from the Applications folder in your home folder.

The app is unsigned and not notarized. If macOS blocks it, open System Settings > Privacy & Security and choose Open Anyway. You can also run bash install.sh in Terminal. Do not turn off Gatekeeper.

On some Macs the F4 mode key needs Fn+F4.

Update the game

Linux managed installs can report their version, update from official source and select the previous verified installation. Windows/macOS still use source reinstall; managed update and rollback on those platforms remain unfinished.

  1. Save your world and close the game when convenient. Updating does not restart a running session; reopen afterwards to use the new release.
  2. From a clean official Git checkout, run bash install.sh --version, then bash install.sh --update. After archive setup, use ~/.local/share/voxelgame/app/launch.sh --version and --update instead. For a custom installation, use its launch.sh or the source script with --prefix PATH.
  3. Read the installed and available commit, build progress and final result. Linux needs Python 3.9+, Git, a prepared Rust/compiler toolchain and at least 5 GiB free. The update command does not install prerequisites or ask for administrator access.
  • Worlds, settings, screenshots and editable projects remain in their separate data folders.
  • Updates build official source in isolation and verify the completed files before switching the launcher. Dirty source checkouts cause a refusal; nothing is stashed or reset.
  • If fetching, building or verification fails, keep using the old launcher. Fix the reported network, disk-space or permission problem and retry.
  • Run bash install.sh --rollback to verify and select the previous release. Old releases are retained; updates do not delete them automatically.
  • Logs are under ~/.local/state/voxelgame/update-*.log unless the log folder was overridden.
Careful. Keep backups. Rollback switches application files only. An older executable may refuse worlds saved in a newer format; rollback does not undo changes to worlds or settings. Linux headless session preservation was checked; Windows/macOS parity and both-computer delivery remain pending.

On Windows/macOS, close the game, extract the newer source and rerun the installer. Their existing separate data folders are preserved; verified managed rollback is Linux only.

Where the files are

Key or actionWhat it does
LinuxWorlds and editable data: ~/.local/share/voxelgame/data. Installer logs: ~/.local/state/voxelgame
macOSWorlds and editable data: ~/Library/Application Support/Voxelgame. Installer logs: ~/Library/Logs/Voxelgame
WindowsWorlds and editable data: %LOCALAPPDATA%\Voxelgame\data. Installer logs: %LOCALAPPDATA%\Voxelgame\logs

On Linux, shared display, audio, controls and accessibility preferences are in $XDG_CONFIG_HOME/voxelgame/settings, defaulting to ~/.config/voxelgame/settings. Mode, environment controls, progression and accepted gameplay configuration remain in the world file. Other platforms have not received native profile-location acceptance.

Setup writes a log once it starts, including runs that fail later. It prints the log path at the start, and a failed run does not repeat it. A stop before setup starts, such as a cancelled plan, leaves no log. Its file name is install-<date>-<id>.log. On Linux and macOS, set VOXELGAME_INSTALL_LOG_DIR to change the log folder.

How worlds are stored

  • Each world is one .vxw file in the worlds folder inside the data folder.
  • Stars from the Worlds page are kept in worlds/favourites.txt, one save path per line, not inside the world file.
  • The starting world is worlds/debug/debug.vxw. The menu lists it as DEBUG.
  • A world with a name is saved in a folder named from the name in lowercase letters, numbers and hyphens, for example worlds/my-island/world.vxw. If that folder already exists, a number is added (my-island-2). A name with no usable letters or numbers gets a numbered folder.
  • A world with an empty name is saved as worlds/world-0001/world.vxw, then world-0002, and so on.

The game stores only your changes. Untouched terrain is generated again from the world's seed. New worlds have no seed field.

Continue opens the starting world

The starting world is always worlds/debug/debug.vxw, so Continue opens DEBUG after every restart. To keep playing another world, open Worlds and load it. Settings are saved per world. The settings you see right after launch belong to DEBUG.

Tip. Close the game before you copy a world file, so the copy holds the latest save. Autosave runs about every 30 seconds after world changes such as building, mining, storage, journal edits or boats.
Careful. The installer does not move worlds from a source checkout started with ./run.sh. Copying that worlds folder into the data folder with the game closed should work, but this is inferred from the save paths and has not been tested.

World mode, generator, time/weather/season controls and progression belong to that world. Display, audio, controls and accessibility preferences are shared across worlds. New saves retain gameplay-compatibility identities; a changed required configuration blocks startup and keeps the save. Use Back, restore the matching configuration, or choose a separate world. Legacy saves acquire these identities after a successful start and save.

Requirements

Linux with a Vulkan graphics driver and an X11 or XWayland session is the tested platform. The Windows (64-bit Intel or AMD, Windows 10 or 11) and macOS (Apple Silicon, or Intel with a Metal GPU) installers are included, but no real machine has checked graphics and sound on them yet. System requirements and supported platforms

The first build needs internet access and several GB of free disk space. The README's 60 FPS target assumes at least an integrated GPU. Software Vulkan (llvmpipe) is only for diagnostics.

Uninstall

There is no uninstaller. Delete the app folder and its launcher by hand. Uninstalling

  • Linux: delete the app folder, `~/.local/share/voxelgame/app` by default, and `~/.local/share/applications/voxelgame.desktop`.
  • macOS: delete `~/Applications/Voxelgame.app`.
  • Windows: delete the app folder and the Voxelgame shortcut in your Start menu Programs folder. The FFmpeg copy in `%LOCALAPPDATA%\Voxelgame\tools` stays unless you delete it too.
  • Compilers, Rust, Homebrew and audio tools that setup installed stay on the PC.
Careful. Your worlds stay in the data folder until you delete it. Deleting the data folder removes all worlds for good, so copy any world you want to keep first.

Build from source

Developers can build the game without the installer. With Rust 1.75 or newer and the Linux packages installed, run `cargo run --release --locked --bin voxelgame`, or `./run.sh`. Build and run from source (cargo or ./run.sh)

  • `run.sh` rebuilds only when sources, assets or Cargo files are newer than the program. It shows a small Preparing the game window while it builds.
  • Started this way, worlds live in the worlds folder inside the source folder.
  • Optional: `aplay` (alsa-utils) for sound and `ffmpeg` for music.

The Linux menu entry and the macOS app use the Voxelgame cube icon. The Windows Start menu shortcut and the game window have no icon. App and launcher icon
